package.name: vi_planner
package.description:
Unified value-iteration planner for Nav2: a single Rust node that serves BOTH the compute_path_to_pose and follow_path actions (nav2_msgs) from ONE value function. Replaces nav2_planner's planner_server and nav2_controller's controller_server at the same time, so a goal is solved once instead of twice (as it was when vi_global_planner and vi_local_planner ran side by side). The global path is a greedy rollout of the solved value function; the local control loop refines the same value function inside a moving +-1m window with laser-scan penalties and publishes the greedy action as cmd_vel.
Because both actions read the same ValueIterator::states, what the local window learns from the laser is visible to the global rollout -- but only after it is propagated: the windowed refinement sweeps the +-1m window and stops there, so a blocked corridor stays invisible to a rollout descending from 20m away. global_sweep (on by default) closes that loop by sweeping the whole shared field with Gauss-Seidel in the background, in chunks that yield the lock so the 10Hz follow loop keeps running.
map_scale and the out-of-core (compact) solver are both supported, but a compact solve never allocates states -- the follow loop hydrates only a patch around the robot from the sink, and that patch is discarded on every recenter. So there is no shared field under compact and global_sweep does nothing; prefer a dense solver with map_scale sized to fit (dense costs 80 B/state: 56 for states plus 24 for sweep_orders, and dense_limit_mb refuses to start above the limit). compact_ram_limit_mb spills the compact sink to disk when compact_sink_dir is unset and it would not fit in RAM.
